Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Why do people hate M. Night Shyamalan so much? What makes him such a bad director in your opinion?
Answer: I think the biggest reason why people dislike (hate seems a bit much here) M. Night Shyamalan is that they expect a stunning plot twist in every one of his movies. And when the plot twist comes, they usually don’t like it, or they bemoan that the twist was too easy to guess. M.N.S’ first three big budget movies were great - Sixth Sense, Unbreakable, and Signs are all great flicks, and fun to watch even today. Then came the massive stinker, The Village. That movie had a horrid plot twist, which spoiled the entire movie. Then came Lady in the Water, The Happening, The Last Airbender, and (oh boy!) After Earth. Four stinkers in a row, and three with dumb plot twists, which would have been easy to spot, a mile away, by a deaf, mute, and blind viewer. My guess is that these four flops perhaps really destroyed his reputation. Since then, he’s improved a bit, or at least, tried to go back, somewhat, to the good old times of his initial trio of successes. I quite enjoyed The Visit, Split, and Glass, but found that Old had a ludicrous plot twist of its own. So anyway, I don’t think he’s a bad director - just that sometimes his direction is rather predictable. When it’s not, when the twist works, his direction isn’t to be faulted. It’s only when the twist fails, when his direction gets hauled over the coals. So, I would argue that his directorial abilities are proportional to his script writing prowess. When his story or script is weak, then the resultant movie seems like it is poorly directed. Anyway, in recent times, I really enjoyed The Visit. It had a fabulous twist, and is a rather good movie.

Question: What character do you think would scare the Joker in a confrontation?
Answer: I think they depicted this in an actual comic - The Punisher quite scared the Joker, and then, Batsie had to come save the Clown Prince from The Punisher. I’m just not sure whether this comic is canon or not. I think this would be pretty accurate though. With Batman, Joker knows that Batsie will never kill him. He will be off for a little holiday in Arkham Asylum, and then back to causing chaos soon after. NO Chance of that ever happening with only Frank Castle involved. One bullet (or many), and it’s bye-bye Joker. And, he knows it! Another person that could possibly scare the Joker is Billy Butcher from Boys - but I’m not so sure really. Billy Butcher would probably recruit the Joker into his squad. So, I guess, Frank Castle as the Punisher, remains my pick for this question.

Answer: It’s bloody awful! The MCU has butchered the look of Gorr the God Butcher! Who the F cares that it’s Christian Bale playing Gorr, if he doesn’t look like Gorr? Question: What was the reason for the feud between Hrithik Roshan and Aamir Khan over the success of the film Kites?
Answer: My gosh, QPG - you have certainly opened some old wounds and made them fresh again. The fearsome feud between Hrithik and Aamir over Kites really does bring back some tender memories. So, the way it went was that Hrithik invited Aamir over for a screening of Kites - Aamir misunderstood the invite, and turned up in a traditional garb with a Desi Kite. Imagine the utter confusion when Hrithik wanted to impress his costar Barbara Mori, but here comes Aamir with a Desi Kite. Sadly, the misunderstanding caused a real Kati Patang situation in the burgeoning friendship of Hrithik and Aamir. Sadly, later on, things became even worse, when Aamir invited Hrithik over to his movie Dhobi Ghat, Hrithik ended up spending a harrowing hour frantically running through the real Dhobi Ghat to avoid a frenzied mob of glistening dhobis. Unlike the QPG, human readers will obviously understand that the above is pure fantasy - no such feud happened, and how could it? Kites was not a success, and despite all the effort that went into it, the movie was a flop. It did create a rift in Hrithik’s marriage though, thanks to a reported affair between him and Barbara Mori. But Aamir Khan was probably not in the slightest bit affected by the fate of Kites, and as far as I can tell, he has never feuded with Hrithik Roshan over anything at all.
